vitest.config.ts View all files Repository files navigation README Contributing MIT license Security More items Apify MCP server Connect your agent to the largest marketplace of tools for AI. The official Apify Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives AI agents web scraping, data extraction, and browser automation through thousands of ready-made Actors from Apify Store , at https://mcp.apify.com . Apify is the marketplace of ready-to-run tools for AI agents. One connection to the Apify MCP server gives your agent thousands of tools to choose from, for jobs like web fetch, SERP monitoring, lead generation and enrichment, and pulling data from e-commerce sites and social media. The server loads only what each task needs. Your agent searches Apify Store, checks an Actor's input and pricing, runs it, and reads the structured results, so you don't install a separate MCP server for every site. Connect to the hosted server with OAuth, or run it locally over stdio with the @apify/actors-mcp-server npm package. Contents Quickstart Set up your client Remote (hosted) or local MCP server How an agent uses Apify Actors Tools, resources, and prompts Choose which tools load UI mode configuration Example prompts Pricing and limits Telemetry Troubleshooting and limitations FAQ Development Contributing Privacy and license Learn more 🚀 Quickstart Open the MCP configurator , pick your client, and choose the tools you want. Copy the generated configuration, deeplink, or command into your client. Sign in to Apify in the browser window that opens. If you don't have an account, you can create a free one there. The hosted endpoint is https://mcp.apify.com . If your client can't use OAuth, send your Apify API token in an Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN> header instead. Treat the token like a password and keep it out of repositories. Create a token in Apify Console and copy it right after creating it. It is shown only once. Using a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot? An official Apify plugin installs this MCP server together with Apify agent skills in one step. 🤖 Set up your client The configurator generates the exact setup for each supported client, including Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude, Claude Desktop, Codex, OpenCode, Kiro, and more. The snippets below cover the most common cases. Claude Code claude mcp add apify " https://mcp.apify.com " -t http Claude Code opens the Apify sign-in page the first time it uses the server. To install the Apify plugin with Apify agent skills instead, run /plugin marketplace add apify/apify-claude-code-plugin , then /plugin install apify@apify and /reload-plugins . ChatGPT Open ChatGPT Plugins , select Add in the top-right corner, then Add custom MCP server . Fill in the form: Icon : upload the Apify icon . Name : Apify Description : Extract data from any website with thousands of scrapers, crawlers, and automations on Apify Store Connection : Server URL , the URL with your settings from the configurator , for example with ?tools= . Without custom settings, use https://mcp.apify.com . Authentication : OAuth Check I understand and want to continue , then select Create as a plugin . Sign in with Apify, review the tools, and install the plugin. No API token is needed. Start a new conversation, type @ , and select Apify . In Business, Enterprise, and Edu workspaces, an admin or owner may need to create or publish the plugin. If the option is missing, ask your workspace admin. When the server's tools change, open the plugin and select Refresh . The ChatGPT desktop app uses local MCP configuration shared with Codex instead: go to Settings > MCP servers > Add server , choose Streamable HTTP, and enter https://mcp.apify.com . See OpenAI's custom MCP server guide . Cursor Add Apify to Cursor , or let the Apify CLI write the configuration, including your API token: apify mcp install cursor The same command works for claude-code , vscode , codex , kiro , and antigravity . VS Code and GitHub Copilot Use the one-click install link from the configurator , run apify mcp install vscode , or add https://mcp.apify.com as an HTTP server in your MCP configuration: { "servers" : { "apify" : { "type" : " http " , "url" : " https://mcp.apify.com " } } } Claude Add Apify to Claude : the link opens the custom connector dialog with the name and URL filled in. Sign in with Apify when prompted. To set it up by hand, open Settings > Connectors , select Add custom connector , name it Apify , and enter https://mcp.apify.com as the remote MCP server URL. The same connector works on Claude.ai and in Claude Desktop. See the Claude guide . Any other MCP client (JSON config) Most clients that support remote servers and OAuth accept a configuration like this: { "mcpServers" : { "apify" : { "url" : " https://mcp.apify.com " } } } Local stdio (npx) Requires Node.js 22 or later. { "mcpServers" : { "actors-mcp-server" : { "command" : " npx " , "args" : [ " -y " , " @apify/actors-mcp-server " ], "env" : { "APIFY_TOKEN" : " YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN " } } } } Create an API token in Apify Console and copy it right after creating it. It is shown only once. If you've run apify login , the server can also read the token saved by the Apify CLI. Run npx @apify/actors-mcp-server --help for all options. The server is also listed in the Docker MCP catalog , and each release ships an MCP bundle file ( apify-mcp-server.mcpb ) for one-click installation in clients that support it. Remote (hosted) or local MCP server The hosted remote MCP server with OAuth is the recommended option. Use the local server when you want to run the MCP process on your own machine; Actors still run and store their results on the Apify platform in both modes. If your client supports only stdio, you can also bridge it to the hosted server with mcp-remote : npx mcp-remote https://mcp.apify.com . Hosted ( https://mcp.apify.com ) Local ( npx @apify/actors-mcp-server ) Transport Streamable HTTP stdio Authentication OAuth or Bearer token APIFY_TOKEN environment variable or Apify CLI login Output schemas inferred for Actor results Yes No Tool selection tools URL parameter --tools flag or TOOLS environment variable Updates Always the latest server The npm version you install How an agent uses Apify Actors Actors are serverless programs on the Apify platform. Each one does a specific job, like scraping Google Maps, crawling a website for RAG, or collecting social media posts. The MCP server turns Actors into tools an agent can find and call without you configuring each one in advance. A typical task follows four steps: search-actors finds candidate Actors in Apify Store for the task. fetch-actor-details returns the Actor's input schema, README, and pricing, plus its output schema on request. call-actor starts the run and waits for it to finish, 30 seconds by default and up to 45. It returns the run status and storage IDs ; the scraped items stay in the run's dataset. get-dataset-items reads the results from the run's dataset, with limit and offset for pagination. The server adds get-dataset-items , get-key-value-store-record , get-actor-run , and abort-actor-run whenever call-actor or an Actor tool is loaded, so the agent can always read results and check on long runs that outlast the wait. You can also expose a specific Actor as its own tool, for example apify/instagram-scraper . The server builds the tool's parameters from the Actor's input schema, so the agent knows exactly what to pass. A Server Actor with an API schema, such as apify/web-fetch , apify/web-search , or apify/rag-web-browser , gets a tool that sends one HTTP request to its API instead. Actors that run their own MCP server. Some Actors are MCP servers themselves. fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list lists their tools, and call-actor-mcp-tool calls one. When such an Actor is loaded as a tool source and has no API schema, its tools are exposed under names in the form username--actor-name--tool-name ; an Actor with an API schema, such as apify/web-search , gets its server tool instead, and call-actor-mcp-tool reaches its MCP tools. Apify Store also lists MCP-related Actors from independent creators; those are separate products with their own READMEs and pricing. 🛠️ Tools, resources, and prompts Any Actor can be a tool, and agents discover new ones as they work. By default, the server loads the actors and docs categories, two Actor tools ( Web Search and Web Fetch ), and report-problem . Everything else is opt-in by category or by tool name. Helper tools Besides Actor tools, the server provides helper tools for the Apify platform: Actors: search Apify Store, list the Actors in your account, view their details, call tools on Actors that run MCP servers, send requests to Server Actors, and delete your own Actors. Documentation: search the Apify and Crawlee docs and fetch pages as context. Runs and storage: list runs, inspect them, read their logs, and read datasets and key-value stores. Tasks and schedules: manage saved Actor tasks and their public landing pages, and schedules that run Actors and tasks automatically. Builds and versions: build Actors, read build logs, and create, read, change, copy, and delete versions from files. Apify API: search the API reference, inspect an operation, and send requests to read or change data. Available tools Legend for the Enabled by default column: ✅ In the default tool set. ⚡ Added automatically when call-actor , an Actor tool, or get-actor-run is loaded, which is true in the default configuration. ✅¹ Served by default only when telemetry is on and the client name doesn't contain claude , anthropic , or local-agent-mode . Select it explicitly with tools=report-problem or tools=dev to serve it to any client; telemetry still has to be on. Tool name Category Description Enabled by default search-actors actors Search for Actors in Apify Store. ✅ fetch-actor-details actors Get an Actor's input schema, README (summary when available, full otherwise), pricing, and a Server Actor's HTTP operations. The output schema is opt-in. ✅ call-actor actors Run an Actor and return its run status and storage IDs. Use fetch-actor-details first to get the input schema. ✅ fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list actors List the tools of an Actor that runs an MCP server, with their schemas, annotations, and metadata. ✅ call-actor-mcp-tool actors Call one tool on an Actor's MCP server and return its result. ✅ send-server-actor-request actors Send one HTTP request to a Server Actor's API, as documented by its API schema, and return the response. ✅ get-actor-run runs Get details about an Actor run. ⚡ get-dataset-items storage Read items from a dataset, with filtering and pagination. ⚡ get-key-value-store-record storage Get the value stored under a key in a key-value store. ⚡ abort-actor-run runs Abort a running Actor run, optionally gracefully. ⚡ search-apify-docs docs Search the Apify and Crawlee documentation for relevant pages. ✅ fetch-apify-docs docs Fetch the full content of a documentation page by its URL. ✅ apify--web-search Actor (see Choose which tools load ) Search the web and return one page of results: titles, URLs, and snippets. ✅ apify--web-fetch Actor (see Choose which tools load ) Fetch a URL and return its content as Markdown, text, HTML, or other formats. ✅ report-problem dev Report a problem with an Apify tool or Actor to the Apify team. ✅¹ apify--rag-web-browser Actor (see Choose which tools load ) Search the web and return the content of the top results. get-actor-list none (select by name: tools=get-actor-list ) List the Actors you own and those shared with you, including private ones. delete-actor none (select by name: tools=delete-actor ) Delete an Actor from your account permanently. key-value store. get-key-value-store-keys storage List the keys in a key-value store. get-key-value-store-list storage List the key-value stores in your account. create-actor-task tasks Create a saved Actor task (a named, reusable Actor configuration). get-actor-task tasks Get a saved Actor task, its publication state, and its public display configuration. update-actor-task tasks Update a task's input, run options, or public display configuration. publish-actor-task tasks Publish a task on its public landing page. unpublish-actor-task tasks Unpublish a task from its public landing page. create-schedule schedules Create a schedule that runs Actors or tasks on a cron expression. get-schedule schedules Get a schedule, its cron expression, state, and the actions it runs. update-schedule the build to finish. get-actor-build builds Get the status of an Actor build. get-actor-build-list builds List the account's builds, or one Actor's, in every status, newest first. get-actor-build-log builds Read the log of an Actor build. get-actor-version versions Get an Actor version's file listing with hashes, plus the content of the files you ask for. create-actor versions Create a private Actor in your account from files, optionally starting a build. update-actor-version versions Write, edit, or delete files of an Actor version in one all-or-nothing write. create-actor-version versions Add a version to an Actor, from files or as a copy of another version, optionally starting a build. delete-actor-version versions Delete an Actor version. Its builds and their tags stay. apify-api-search api Search the Apify API reference by keywords. Returns each operation's method, path, and docs page. apify-api-details api Get the parameters and request body schema of the Apify API operations on a path. apify-api-read api Send a GET request to an Apify API path, like apify api in the Apify CLI. It refuses GETs to the synchronous run endpoints, which start a paid run. apify-api-write api Send a POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE request with a JSON body to any Apify API path, like apify api in the Apify CLI. The tasks category manages saved Actor tasks . It is unrelated to the MCP Tasks protocol. The tool reference has full descriptions of each tool. Tool annotations Every tool carries a title , a readOnlyHint , and an openWorldHint . readOnlyHint is true for tools that only read data. Actor tools get it only for Apify-maintained Actors with limited permissions and no inputs that accept secrets, writable storage, an MCP connector, or code; other Actor tools are marked destructive. openWorldHint is true for tools that reach outside the Apify platform, such as call-actor , and false for platform-only tools. Prompts and resources No prompts are registered yet, so prompts/list returns an empty list. resources/read accepts any Apify API GET URL ( https://api.apify.com/v2/... ) and returns the response body using the session's Apify token, inlined up to 256 KB. Your data isn't enumerated in resources/list ; resources/templates/list lists the common shapes with their paging parameters. Choose which tools load The tools parameter takes categories, tool names, and Actor names, separated by commas. When you set it, the defaults are dropped and only what you list is loaded, plus the ⚡ run and storage tools whenever the list includes call-actor or an Actor. The easiest way to build a selection is the configurator . Hosted server: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=actors,docs,apify/web-search,apify/web-fetch Local server: npx @apify/actors-mcp-server --tools actors,docs,apify/web-search,apify/web-fetch To give an agent a single Actor, list only that Actor. The agent gets its tool plus the four ⚡ tools it needs to read the results: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=apify/instagram-scraper Pin your tools in production. The default tool set can change between versions. Set tools explicitly if you need a stable interface. Backward compatibility with older configurations apify/web-search replaced apify/rag-web-browser in the default tools. To keep apify--rag-web-browser , add apify/rag-web-browser to your tools list, or set tools=actors,docs,apify/rag-web-browser,apify/web-fetch for the previous default categories and Actors. The actors URL parameter and --actors flag still work. They're merged into tools , so ?actors=apify/web-fetch equals ?tools=apify/web-fetch . enableAddingActors , enable-adding-actors , and enableActorAutoLoading were removed and are ignored. Dynamic Actor calls come from call-actor , which the default actors category includes. The selectors add-actor , experimental , and preview are retired and load nothing. Use call-actor or the actors category. get-actor-log was renamed to get-actor-run-log , and the source category to versions . The old names load nothing. call-actor no longer calls tools on MCP server Actors: the actorName:toolName form is rejected. Use call-actor-mcp-tool with actor , tool , and arguments . call-actor still starts a run of an MCP server Actor that has an input schema; one without is refused. A selection that names call-actor alone needs call-actor-mcp-tool added. fetch-actor-details no longer lists an MCP server Actor's tools, and output.mcpTools is ignored. Use fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list , which returns the definitions in structuredContent.tools . A selection that names fetch-actor-details alone needs fetch-actor-mcp-tool-list added. A selected Actor with an API schema (a Server Actor) gets a tool that sends one HTTP request to its API, with method , path , and query arguments, instead of a tool that starts a run. If the Actor is also an MCP server, the selection no longer loads its MCP tools: use call-actor-mcp-tool . call-actor still starts runs of the Actor when it has an input schema. A selected apify/rag-web-browser is served this way too, with GET /search . apify--web-fetch sends one HTTP request to the Web Fetch Actor's API instead of starting a run, and returns the HTTP response. Its arguments are method , path , query and, for POST / , body , for example {"method": "GET", "path": "/", "query": {"url": "https://example.com", "formats": ["markdown", "links"]}} . apify--web-search sends one HTTP request to the Web Search Actor's API instead of starting a run, and returns the HTTP response. Its arguments are method , path , query and, for POST / , body , for example {"method": "GET", "path": "/", "query": {"query": "AI agent payment protocols", "maxResults": 5}} . call-actor still starts runs of the Actor, and call-actor-mcp-tool calls its search MCP tool. UI mode configuration The ui parameter controls MCP Apps widget tools. With UI mode on, the server adds search-actors-widget and fetch-actor-details-widget next to their base tools, which keep returning standard responses. By default ( auto ), UI mode turns on when the client supports MCP Apps. Value Behavior auto (default) Widget tools added when the client supports MCP Apps true , on , or apps Widget tools always added false , off , or default No widget tools Hosted server: https://mcp.apify.com?tools=actors,docs&ui=true Local server, with a CLI flag or the UI_MODE environment variable: npx @apify/actors-mcp-server --ui true UI_MODE=true npx @apify/actors-mcp-server 💬 Example prompts Ask in plain language. The agent finds a suitable Actor, checks its input and pricing, runs it, and reads the results. These prompts cover the most common jobs: Use case Example prompt Example Actor Web research "Find what people on X said about autonomous AI agents this week and summarize the key developments." Tweet Scraper V2 Search and read the web "Compare the current pricing plans of Notion, Coda, and Airtable and tell me which is cheapest for a 10-person team." "Show me the next 10 results from that run" makes the agent call get-dataset-items again with a higher offset . With the schedules category loaded, "Run that Google Maps search every Monday at 9 am" creates a schedule. 💰 Pricing and limits Connecting to the MCP server is free. Actor runs bill to your Apify account according to each Actor's pricing, which fetch-actor-details shows before a run. The Apify free plan includes $5 of monthly platform usage. To cap what a run can cost, pass maxTotalChargeUsd (pay-per-event Actors) or maxItems (pay-per-result Actors) in the callOptions of call-actor . timeout and memory limit the run's duration and memory, not its price. The hosted server accepts up to 20 requests per second per account. search-actors returns only free and pay-per-event Actors that pass the platform's agent-safety filters, so rental and pay-per-result Actors don't appear in search. Full-permission Actors need your one-time approval; until then, call-actor returns an error with an approval link. Some tools work without an Apify account: search-actors , fetch-actor-details , search-apify-docs , fetch-apify-docs , apify-api-search , and apify-api-details . Select only those, for example https://mcp.apify.com?tools=search-actors , and the hosted server accepts the connection without a token. 🪙 Agentic payments (experimental). Agents can pay for Actor runs without an Apify account. AGI sells a prepaid, spend-capped Apify API token for an x402, MPP, or Skyfire payment. The agent then uses it as a normal Bearer token against mcp.apify.com , with any Actor that uses limited permissions. See the agentic payments documentation for supported methods and limits, and agi.apify.com/AGENTS.md for protocol details. 📡 Telemetry The Apify MCP server collects telemetry about tool calls to help Apify understand usage patterns and improve the service. Telemetry is on by default. With telemetry on, Actor searches in Apify Store send the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 hash of the MCP session ID as _traceId , and tool-call events carry it as trace_id . search-actors also sends _useCase , a one-sentence reason for the search written by the model, which Apify uses to improve Store search results. The stdio transport also uses Sentry for error tracking, which helps the Apify team find and fix issues faster. To opt out, including Sentry, set the telemetry-enabled URL parameter or the --telemetry-enabled CLI flag to false , or set TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false . CLI flags take precedence over environment variables. https://mcp.apify.com?telemetry-enabled=false npx @apify/actors-mcp-server --telemetry-enabled=false TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false npx @apify/actors-mcp-server 🐛 Troubleshooting and limitations The local server won't start. Check your Node.js version: the package requires Node.js 22 or later. Authentication fails. Reconnect so the client repeats the OAuth flow, or switch to a Bearer token. For the local server, check that APIFY_TOKEN is set in the client's server configuration, not only in your shell. VS Code says the OAuth app is not registered. Run Authentication: Remove Dynamic Authentication Providers , select Apify, and sign in again. Client features vary. Any MCP client can connect, but support for dynamic tool lists, OAuth, and MCP Apps differs between clients. Invalid Actor input. When call-actor fails because of invalid input, the error includes the Actor's input schema so the agent can correct the input and retry. How the server adapts Actor input schemas The server adapts Actor input schemas so that more clients and models can use them: Descriptions longer than 500 characters are cut at the last complete sentence and marked [Description truncated] . Enums are kept in full up to 2,000 combined characters. Larger enums are replaced by a short note with example values. Required fields get a REQUIRED prefix in their descriptions for frameworks that ignore the JSON Schema required list. Nested properties are built for special inputs such as proxy configuration and request lists. Missing array item types are inferred from the item type, the prefill, the default value, or the editor type, in that order. Prefill and default values are copied into descriptions as examples, for clients that ignore JSON Schema examples . For more help, see the MCP documentation or open an issue . ❓ FAQ What is an MCP server? An MCP server exposes tools and data to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol , an open standard supported by clients such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. The agent connects once and calls the server's tools when a task needs them. The Apify MCP server's tools are the Actors in Apify Store. What is the Apify MCP server? It's the official Model Context Protocol server for Apify. It lets AI agents search Apify Store, run Actors for web scraping, data extraction, and browser automation, and read the structured results. When is it a good MCP server for web scraping? When an agent needs data from many different sites. A typical case is Google Maps one day, Instagram or an online store the next. The agent picks a ready-made Actor for each site from Apify Store instead of you writing and maintaining a scraper. Each Actor works like a web scraping API for its site, and the Apify platform handles scaling, proxies, and storage of the results. How does it compare to Playwright MCP? Playwright MCP drives a browser on your machine step by step, through clicks and page snapshots. The Apify MCP server runs Actors in the Apify cloud. Each Actor handles JavaScript rendering, proxies, and blocking for its site and returns structured results, so the agent asks for the data instead of operating a browser. Many agents use both. Can ChatGPT or Claude scrape websites with it? Yes. Connect ChatGPT, Claude, or Claude Code to https://mcp.apify.com , then ask in plain language. The model searches for a suitable Actor, runs it, and reads the results. Is it free? Connecting is free, and some discovery tools work without an account. Actor runs bill to your Apify account at each Actor's price, and the free plan includes $5 of monthly platform usage. Do I need an API token? Not with the hosted server, because OAuth signs you in through the browser. The local server needs APIFY_TOKEN or an Apify CLI login. Can I limit what the agent can do or spend? Yes. Select tools with the tools parameter or expose a single Actor. To cap a run's cost, pass maxTotalChargeUsd for pay-per-event Actors or maxItems for pay-per-result Actors in call-actor options. 🔧 Development This repository contains the open-source server package published to npm as @apify/actors-mcp-server . The hosted service at mcp.apify.com runs on this core logic from a separate private repository. You need Node.js 22 or later and pnpm. pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm run dev # Streamable HTTP server on http://localhost:3001, hot reload for widgets pnpm run inspector:stdio # MCP Inspector against the stdio server The development HTTP server doesn't read APIFY_TOKEN from the environment. Pass your token in an Authorization: Bearer header or a ?token= query parameter, for example from the MCP Inspector .
